      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "K1",
      "question": "What constitutes a requester-visible closure notice, and how promptly can the existing delivery path send it?",
      "changes": "Notification content, delivery timing, and the running-server acceptance check.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use a closure message comparable to the resolved message, enqueue it immediately, and deliver on the next enabled worker tick; verify the notifier output rather than assuming the downstream relay delivered email.",
      "blocks": "Notification acceptance criteria until discovery establishes the existing template, worker cadence, and observable delivery boundary."

      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "Which existing lifecycle, pagination, report, notification, and audit behaviors must remain compatible?",
      "changes": "Implementation boundaries and regression tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve the documented lifecycle, cursor contract, report columns, audit semantics, and existing notification behavior; leave retry logic untouched.",
      "blocks": "Compatibility decisions until discovery checks the relevant contracts and tests."
    },

      "id": "Q3",

      "route": "inspect",

      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "For the same ticket and requester, suppress a closure notice when a resolution notice was successfully sent within the preceding five minutes; a pending or failed notice alone does not establish delivery.",

      "id": "Q5",

      "route": "default",

      "route": "inspect",

      "route": "default",

  "summary": "S1 [fact]: The target is the help desk ticket service in this repository. S2 [fact; Q1, Q4]: Closing should notify the requester while avoiding a second recent notice. S3 [fact; Q5]: Delivery should be prompt and bulk closes should avoid spamming recipients. S4 [fact; Q6]: The list API needs a closed-ticket window filter; the inspected weekly report counts current records and does not itself define a time window. S5 [fact]: List filters must intersect as documented. S6 [fact]: Discovery found that matchesFilters currently uses OR, so the documented combined-filter behavior needs correction and verification. S7 [fact; Q12]: A later stage must back-chain before implementation and continue until tests pass and behavior is verified against a running server. S8 [fact; Q16]: Overnight Ralph-style work is optional and must have a cap. S9 [fact]: Tests must demonstrate behavior and documentation must be accurate and concise. S10 [fact]: Outbox retry logic is outside the change; the OldTracker migration is context, not a request to implement migration. S11 [fact]: The service must remain free of external dependencies. S12 [fact; Q7, Q9]: Repeated closes must have no repeated effects while returning 409, and the close audit records the actor. S13 [fact; Q3, Q14]: A single bulk call must handle 500 closes and remain responsive. Discovery leads [hints, not verified authority]: the help desk team and support leads, repository README and API and operations docs, decision records, weekly-report script, existing tests, and the ambiguous terms 'just got one', 'right away', 'batch', and 'weekly window'; no specific external channel, private site, repository, or owner was supplied. Interaction and state [facts and defaults]: agents enter through HTTP and are identified by X-Actor or system; requesters are identified by the ticket requester field; state is shared through the service process and optionally its data file across sessions and restarts, otherwise it ends with the process; existing internal-network access is assumed, and batched notices must not reveal another recipient's tickets. Authority and visibility [fact]: this intake is read-only, starts no server, implements nothing, and authorizes no deployment; the requested repository is the delivery target for later work, an isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, and deployed behavior becomes visible only after release."
